BLOCKER: Residency enforcement is bypassable by configuration: backup/kms/egress are only checked as subsets of the manifest's own self-asserted `allowed_regions`, and the profile is consulted only for home recognition + retention_days. A product can add any region to its manifest `allowed_regions` and pass. The profile must also bound `allowed_regions` (policy-owned allow-list, ⊆ profile regions) — otherwise the gate enforces internal consistency, not residency.
MAJOR: Duplicate Go type/validation definitions (existing `edpsvc` residency types vs new `go/residencymanifest` types) will drift; conformance fixtures validate files, not type-level drift. Extract/reuse one shared Go package consumed by both, per the reuse guardrail and CL-001 ("single writer? register it").

Validator execution failure semantics are unspecified: missing Go toolchain, unreadable/malformed `config/residency-profiles/<home>.json`, or unreadable `residency-policy.json` must fail closed with a distinct code — distinct from `gate_mode=warn`. As designed, a broken toolchain can silently pass deploys.

`config/residency-policy.json` (the `gate_mode` rollback/bypass lever) and the `residency-manifest.json` template are not registered in `config/store-registry.json` with a single owner/change path — only profiles are. One unreviewed edit flips block→warn; register both and require the warn→block transition to be a tracked decision.

Observability is thin: a one-line stderr summary and a JSON report are not queryable. Emit a structured metric/event keyed by error code (and by product) so warn-mode accumulation and the block transition are visible to dashboards/alerts before customers notice.
MINOR: No stable code is reserved for `schema_version` failures or invalid backup/KMS field shapes, yet AC5 requires identical cross-language pass/block outcomes for those cases. Add `RESIDENCY_SCHEMA_VERSION` (and invalid-field codes) to the frozen set now — retrofitting stable codes later is a breaking change.

The IN template hardcodes `home_region: IN`; a product operating elsewhere silently inherits a wrong home until it overrides. After the warn window, make the template home empty (fail-closed) or require explicit per-product acknowledgement.

Python `core.packaging.validate` and Go `cmd/pfresidency` are two writers of residency rules; the design does not name which is authoritative for build vs deploy. State the precedence/authority in `RESIDENCY-MANIFEST-GATE.md` to prevent divergence in fixes.

Design guardrail answers for checklist items 3/8/9 (authz, API surface, tenant isolation) are implicitly N/A but unstated; `core/design_guardrails.py` (CL-008) expects explicit dispositions at design time.
NIT: `scripts/dev/residency_gate.py` re-implements the template-vs-override manifest resolution that `core/packaging.build` already performs; call the existing loader instead of a second precedence implementation.
SUMMARY: Sound fail-closed intent, warn-first rollout, stable error codes, and cross-language conformance plan; language rule respected (Go shipped logic, Python tooling).

Top risks: (1) self-asserted `allowed_regions` makes the compliance gate bypassable by a config edit, (2) unspecified failure semantics when the validator itself breaks, (3) the gate_mode bypass lever lacks ownership registration.
Consolidate the duplicate Go residency types into one shared package and add a metric per error code before Gate 1.5.
